descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-19 Medication Tracker · S13 Nursing Home: visits 1-2-3 — events keep the last two visits, chronic list and a long-standing hold persist

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U15 Nursing Home: medication events are kept for the last two visits; the chronic medication list persists until changed. (UAT 3.6; TFA-94699 Nursing Home line) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress
  • U12 Nursing Home has its own Medications panel, filled from the pre-round (PR #56). (UAT TC-19 ER 9; TFA-92597 AC 3)
  • T5 A long-standing Nursing Home hold (e.g. metformin) still displays correctly months later. (TFA-94655 AC 4)
  • U18 The step mix (starts, holds, stops, dose changes, conditional orders, one-time doses) is dictated across two days and passes in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-19 Steps; UAT 3.3)
  • U20 Server clock for the retention clocks: the 18 h label, the 36 h clears and the Nursing Home visit date that drives last-two-visits follow the server clock; … (UAT 3.8; TFA-94699 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Nursing Home resident: chronic donepezil 10 mg and amlodipine 5 mg; visit 1 adds a Given row (ceftriaxone 1 g IM once), changes amlodipine 5 → 10 ('was: 5'), holds metformin 'poor intake'

When Visit 2 and visit 3 on later days, both silent about these drugs ('Doing well, no complaints.'); after each visit open the Pre-Round Medications panel

Then After visit 2: everything from visit 1 still shown. After visit 3: the Given row from visit 1 is gone; donepezil and amlodipine persist; the amlodipine Changed tag and the metformin Held tag (with its visit-1 date and reason) are recorded and judged only after Q7

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.6 Nursing Home + TFA-94699 Nursing Home line + TFA-94655 AC 4. Q7 is a UAT-vs-ticket conflict (events kept for the last two visits vs a months-old hold that still shows), so the metformin and amlodipine-tag outcomes are recorded, not expected. Main keeps three visits, so 'Given row gone after visit 3' is expected to fail until TFA-94699 lands (gate). …

Where it ran: local manual (time lane, a script does the person's steps); test method TIME · Time / aging (clock moved); lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (manual)

S13 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-19.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; the Allure status was changed by the triage from failed to broken.

Issue type: Ticket not ready for QA · environment local · tickets TFA-92597 ready for qa; TFA-94655 ready for qa; TFA-94699 in progress

After a resident's third visit, the visit-1 'Ceftriaxone 1 g IM once' Given row is still on the Medications panel: three visits are kept, while the UAT says two.

Evidence: Allure 4acc04c2, TIME lane: 3 of 4 cells passed. The only failing cell, U15, is gated 'blocked: TFA-94699 in progress', and the lane marks it as known. The chronic list and the long-standing metformin hold persist; the Held/Changed tags are recorded under Q7.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane manual.

Test method: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved); secondary: AGENT · Browser agent — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: manual.

UAT item: TC-19 Medication Tracker · Section: A4 · Post-Round · Scenario: TC-19/S13

Nursing Home: visits 1-2-3 — events keep the last two visits, chronic list and a long-standing hold persist

Tickets: TFA-92597 Medication Tracker (ready for qa); TFA-94655 Held Medications in Generated Notes Read from Tracker, Not Old-Note Regex (ready for qa); TFA-94699 Data Retention & Purge (in progress)

New local lane manual: status failed in manual/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)).

How it is tested (manual/plan.json, automatable: yes): chromium spec. Resident with chronic donepezil + amlodipine; visit-1 state (ceftriaxone Given, amlodipine 5 → 10 changed 'was: 5', metformin held 'poor intake') seeded with visit-1 stamps two days back and snfVisitDates [D-2]. Visit 2 and visit 3: real pre-round Save Note 'Doing well, no complaints.' through the UI with the browser clock (page.clock) on D-1 and D, so snfVisitDates gets three device days; after each, snf:applyLifecycle and the Pre-Round Medications panel read. Positive control after each Save Note: notesProcessedAt moved and preRoundError empty (aging.ts lastSave.proof), saved in the evidence; the silent-save cells count only when it passes. — Visits are device calendar days of a pre-round Save Note on main; page.clock gives the device day, the server reads stamps only.

Detail:

3/4 judged cells pass, 4 recorded. Fail: after visit 3: the Given row from visit 1 is gone (events kept for the last two visits) [U15; gate: blocked: TFA-94699 in progress]. Recorded: snfVisitDates after visit 3 (three device days expected) = ["Mon Oct 12 2026","Tue Oct 13 2026","Wed Oct 14 2026"] | after visit 3: amlodipine Changed tag (Q7) = {"status":"changed","changeDate":"Oct 12","changedNote":"was: 5"} | after visit 3: metformin Held tag with its visit-1 date and reason (Q7) = {"status":"held","changeDate":"Oct 12","changedNote":"poor intake"} | silent visits 2 and 3: rows re-dated by the save = [].

Product issue: Known (TFA-94699 in progress, U15): after visit 3 the visit-1 'Ceftriaxone 1 g IM once' Given row is still on the resident's Medications panel. Main keeps 3 visits; UAT 3.6 says the last two.

Evidence: 4 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Needs the aging helper (shifting snfVisitDates and row updatedAt back, a test-only internal mutation called with the local stack's admin key) and legs; dev has no admin key and its server clock cannot be moved, so this stays on the local stack (when the helper exists).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
